verses.english: This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.

verses.pali: Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā.

verses.english: Pleasant feeling should be seen as suffering.
Painful feeling should be seen as a dart.
Neutral feeling should be seen as impermanent.

verses.pali: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sukhā vedanā dukkhato diṭṭhā hoti, dukkhā vedanā sallato diṭṭhā hoti, adukkhamasukhā vedanā aniccato diṭṭhā hoti;
verses.english: When a mendicant has seen these three feelings in this way,

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu ariyo, sammaddaso, acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā’”ti.
verses.english: they’re called a noble mendicant who sees rightly, has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”
“A mendicant who sees pleasure as pain,
And when freed in regards to that,
that peaceful sage, with perfect insight,

verses.pali: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
verses.english: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
